report:
Fresh review after the source_representation annotation was added to complete_claim_blocks_are_selected_but_unrelated_movement_is_not_stale and check.rs gained diagnostic associations/line movement. Compared complete initial fragments: claim, review.rs implementation and the second test remain identical; the first test has only that additional annotation and all previously inspected assertions remain. Recaptured the fixture helpers, shared spec.rs parser (identical to the earlier capture), and the current check_reviews context. These changes preserve the following independently reassessed rationale.

Reviewed the complete selector_claim claim, the single ordinary implementation association in review.rs, and both ordinary associated tests; there are no TODO/N/A entries. Requirements are selection by full dotted identity within the specified source, complete shared normalized claim text rather than the containing document, identity-only selector storage, and freshness across unrelated preceding-line movement.

Implementation: Selector::Claim contains only anchor_id. inventory creates initial claim fragments from SpecAnchor.content with the source path and ID; select loads the same SpecIndex, rejects invalid/ambiguous inventories and absent IDs, verifies the resolved claim source path equals the requested file, and returns claim.content. Captured spec.rs shows the shared parser closes claims at headings, next definitions, explicit ends and source end, preserves internal content while trimming its edges, and dedents Sage prose before parsing. Thus selectors use the shared normalized content instead of inventing another boundary algorithm. input_errors compares initial fragments to the current inventory and reselects declared reads, comparing exact text; neither claim selector nor claim content stores location offsets. The review.rs whole-file snapshot covers this orchestration; captured shared-parser context preserves its additional dependency.

Test sufficiency considered as a complete set: complete_claim_blocks_are_selected_but_unrelated_movement_is_not_stale asserts exact multiline content including paragraphs, emphasis, list, table, and fenced code, records a report, then asserts that preceding blank lines and changes outside the explicit boundary leave validation valid. Its four subsequent internal mutations each assert invalidity. declared_claim_read_tracks_selected_text_without_capturing_the_document exercises the actual additional-read selector using a full dotted ID, checks exact returned claim text and the saved fragment, records, then asserts that a new preceding heading remains valid while changing the claim is invalid. Together these exercise initial and additional claim selection, normalized text, exclusion of the document, movement stability, and meaningful stale detection. A selector that captured the document or depended on old locations would fail these assertions; truncating later claim blocks would fail the exact body and mutation checks. Separate tests for every parser boundary or selector field are not needed for this selector-level integration contract, whose implementation delegates to the shared parser.

Captured Fixture setup/helpers establish a real isolated Cargo workspace, documented claim, ordinary implementation and annotated test, persisted review input access, and report generation; assertions remain visible in the associated test bodies. Captured check.rs confirms validation feeds the checking path. No production or test files were edited and no behavioral bug was identified. I executed review start and recorded reads and inspected their contents; no test suite or cargo build was executed by me. Coordinator now separately reports 331 passing functional sage-meta tests, 46 passing sage-stash tests, and a passing workspace build; those reports are not represented as my own execution. This is a source completeness and test adequacy assessment, independent of those execution results.
